channel.title: Signal//log
channel.description: A running transmission of half-formed thoughts, sketched before they cool into language. Pages that perform their ideas instead of explaining them.

item.title: Vector
item.description: Ideas are viruses and minds are hosts. Five ideas loose in the same population of minds at once — one slow to start and unstoppable once it has company, one that spreads like fire until minds tire of it, one that burns out fast, one that lingers in the gaps. They compete for the same hosts, mutate as they travel, and the strongest is rarely the truest. Drag to orbit, arm an idea, click a mind to plant it.

item.title: Tech and Feelings
item.description: The photo made us feel something. Video made us feel more. Music told us what to feel. Everything attempted since — apps that vibrate the phone on the beat, lights pulsing with the track, smell — adds a sensation while the song plays and stays separate from it. On eye and pulse tracking read back by the feed, a branch of the vagus nerve under the skin of the outer ear, the warmth of someone watching at the same time, and why nobody has found the next one yet.

item.title: The Well-Lit Room
item.description: Smart people make terrible decisions at a rate that should embarrass the idea of smartness. Not because the thinking is weak, but because it is pointed at the only part of the room with a light on. On the problems that can be scored, the ones that never are, and why intelligence is the lawyer rather than the judge.

item.title: The Accidental Eden
item.description: Are we truly capable of solving planetary crises like climate change through top-down master design, or are humanity's greatest breakthroughs born of serendipity? A three-act transmission on Pleistocene climate violence, the Holocene sanctuary, and the two branching futures waiting at the thermostat.

item.title: The Database in the Room
item.description: You can't query the future — SELECT future FROM llm just returns NULL. So hold the model beside something we already know: the database. Once the loud frontier of the '90s wars, now load-bearing furniture no one notices. Not a forecast — a mirror. And the winners weren't Oracle; they were Postgres and SQLite, the engines that won by vanishing.

item.title: The Only Visitor
item.description: On a blog that counts nothing and keeps nothing, and the single, unsaved trace it can still draw: that for a few seconds, someone stayed.

item.title: The Patient Fire
item.description: On biology as the hidden engine of history — that the great deed was a symptom, and the chemistry a person never chose was the hand that built the empire, or the watch.

item.title: Regression to the Mean
item.description: On the machine we were promised would explode the space of ideas — and why a tool that returns the most probable answer may quietly pull everyone toward the average, flagging each genuinely new thing as a mistake.

item.title: Ten Thousand Towers
item.description: On the promise that AI will let anyone build the next big thing — and why cheap creation may scatter us into a plain of weekend-high towers, each speaking its own tongue.

item.title: Born Hollow
item.description: On the small absence we are each born with, the lifelong work of trying to fill it — and why it was never a hole to fix, but a hollow made to sound.

item.title: The Zero-Trust Society
item.description: On a society that has run out of trust — and why the repair is not to rebuild it, but to make it something you no longer need.

item.title: Silent Timelines Echo
item.description: On the feeling that rhymes with nostalgia but arrives when you imagine a future you will never live — and miss it anyway.

item.title: The Flock Problem
item.description: On why smart people with good ideas rarely end up working on the same hard thing — and what moves the flock when it finally moves.

item.title: The Builders' Atlas
item.description: On the map a company never drew of itself — and the agent patient enough to walk it.

item.title: The Continuous Experiment
item.description: If every life is already an experiment — anonymous, ambient, distributed — what would we finally be able to see?

item.title: The Shrinking Spectrum
item.description: On how the cone of possible futures narrows with age — and why what remains is not less.
